sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: It was a cold day in Appalachia on January 7, 1865.
sentences.zh: 1865年1月7日，阿巴拉契亚地区天气寒冷。

sentences.en: A Union soldier named Asa McCoy was on his way home,
sentences.zh: 一位名叫阿萨·麦考伊的联邦士兵正在回家的路上，

sentences.en: wounded from fighting in the Civil War.
As he neared his cabin in Kentucky, Asa was given a message.
sentences.zh: 当他快到肯塔基州的木屋时，有人给了他一条口信。

sentences.en: Don't return home, or you will be killed.
sentences.zh: 别回家，否则你会没命的。

sentences.en: A local group of Confederate militia, known as the Logan Wildcats,
sentences.zh: 当地一个名为“洛根野猫”的邦联民兵组织，

sentences.en: The Wildcats were led by a member of the Hatfields,
sentences.zh: “野猫”组织的头目是哈特菲尔德家族的一员，

sentences.en: a family living in West Virginia who had strong ties to the Confederate Army.
sentences.zh: 这个家族住在西弗吉尼亚州，与邦联军队关系密切。

sentences.en: Asa hid out in a cave near Peter Creek, Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 阿萨躲进了肯塔基州彼得溪附近的一个洞穴里。

sentences.en: He was eventually tracked down and shot dead.
sentences.zh: 他最终还是被追踪到并被枪杀了。

sentences.en: The incident is said to have sparked a famous feud between the Hatfields and the McCoys.
sentences.zh: 据说这起事件引发了哈特菲尔德家族和麦考伊家族之间著名的世仇。
这场世仇持续了几十年。

sentences.en: In 1873, a McCoy family member, perhaps still seething from Asa's death,
sentences.zh: 1873年，一位麦考伊家族成员，或许仍对阿萨的死耿耿于怀，

sentences.en: accused Floyd Hatfield of stealing his pig.
sentences.zh: 指控弗洛伊德·哈特菲尔德偷了他的猪。

sentences.en: A trial followed, and Floyd Hatfield was acquitted.
sentences.zh: 随后进行了审判，弗洛伊德·哈特菲尔德被判无罪。

sentences.en: A few years later, one of the trial witnesses was killed by two McCoys.
sentences.zh: 几年后，其中一名审判证人被两名麦考伊家族成员杀害。

sentences.en: In 1882, on Election Day in Kentucky,
sentences.zh: 1882年，在肯塔基州的选举日当天，

sentences.en: some McCoy brothers drunkenly fought and killed Ellison Hatfield,
sentences.zh: 几名麦考伊兄弟酒后与埃利森·哈特菲尔德发生争执并将其杀害，

sentences.en: stabbing him multiple times in the back.
sentences.zh: 他们朝他的背部连捅数刀。

sentences.en: In retaliation, the Hatfields killed all three McCoy brothers.
sentences.zh: 作为报复，哈特菲尔德家族杀死了那三名麦考伊兄弟。

sentences.en: The feud continued into a cycle of violence that reached its peak in 1888,
sentences.zh: 这场世仇演变成了一场暴力循环，并在1888年达到顶峰，

sentences.en: during what came to be known as the New Year's Night Massacre.
sentences.zh: 也就是后来被称为“新年夜大屠杀”的事件期间。

sentences.en: Several members of the Hatfield gang set fire to a McCoy cabin and killed two children.
sentences.zh: 哈特菲尔德团伙的几名成员放火烧毁了麦考伊家的一间木屋，并杀死了两个孩子。

sentences.en: History is full of incidents that have sparked long-standing grudges,
sentences.zh: 历史上充满了引发长期积怨的事件，

sentences.en: sometimes with consequences that last decades.
sentences.zh: 有时后果会持续几十年。

sentences.en: But there also are smaller, more personal grievances that we all harbor.
sentences.zh: 但我们每个人心中也怀有更细微、更私人的怨恨。

sentences.en: Perhaps you still remember some slight you experienced years ago
sentences.zh: 也许你还记得多年前经历过的某种轻视，

sentences.en: at the hands of a friend or family member?
sentences.zh: 来自朋友或家人的伤害？

sentences.en: Today, we explore the psychology of grudges,
sentences.zh: 今天，我们来探讨怨恨的心理学，

sentences.en: how long-standing animosities affect our lives,
sentences.zh: 长期的敌意如何影响我们的生活，

sentences.en: and what to do about them.
Don't let people live rent-free in your head.
sentences.zh: 别让那些人免费住进你的脑子里。

sentences.en: That's a way of saying you shouldn't allow people who have wronged you
sentences.zh: 这句话的意思是，你不应该让那些伤害过你的人

sentences.en: to take up too much of your attention.
Sounds nice, but is it realistic?
sentences.zh: 听起来不错，但这现实吗？

sentences.en: We are social creatures, after all,
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我们是社会性动物，

sentences.en: and our interactions and relationships with others matter.
sentences.zh: 我们与他人的互动和关系至关重要。

sentences.en: When someone is kind to us, it has the power to alter our day,
sentences.zh: 当有人对我们友善时，它有能力改变我们的一天，

sentences.en: maybe even change the course of our lives.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能改变我们的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: When someone wrongs us, it can also have large effects.
sentences.zh: 当有人伤害我们时，它也会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, Fred Luskin has spent a quarter century
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，弗雷德·拉斯金花了四分之一个世纪

sentences.en: studying what happens when we hold on to grudges.
sentences.zh: 研究当我们怀恨在心时会发生什么。

sentences.en: Fred Luskin, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德·拉斯金，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Fred, some years ago, you met a woman named Debbie.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，几年前，你遇到了一位名叫黛比的女士。

sentences.en: She was having issues with her husband.
sentences.zh: 她和丈夫之间出了些问题。

sentences.en: And when I say issues, this was not merely conflicts about who takes out the garbage.
sentences.zh: 当我说“问题”时，这不仅仅是关于谁去倒垃圾之类的冲突。

sentences.en: I mean, issues, that's a nice way of putting it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，用“问题”来形容已经是很客气的说法了。

sentences.en: Her husband was a serial adulterer.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫是个惯性出轨者。

sentences.en: She had found him cheating numerous times.
sentences.zh: 她发现他多次背叛婚姻。

sentences.en: She said, okay, I'll take you back.
The cycle repeated itself over and over.
sentences.zh: 这个循环一次又一次地重复。

sentences.en: One day, Debbie came home early from work.
sentences.zh: 有一天，黛比提前下班回家。

sentences.en: She discovered her husband on the couch with another woman.
sentences.zh: 她发现丈夫和另一个女人在沙发上。
这是压死骆驼的最后一根稻草。
她内心有什么东西断了。

sentences.en: You'll never treat me like this again.
sentences.zh: 你再也不会这样对待我了。

sentences.en: But when we met her, this guy owned her brain.
sentences.zh: 但当我们见到她时，这个男人依然占据着她的头脑。

sentences.en: And her conversation was just so dominated by him, him, him, him, him.
sentences.zh: 她的谈话内容完全被他、他、他、他、他所支配。

sentences.en: So many people have been in similar situations where they have been betrayed by a romantic partner.
sentences.zh: 很多人都有过类似的经历，被浪漫伴侣背叛。

sentences.en: And people really struggle with it.
sentences.zh: 人们真的为此挣扎不已。

sentences.en: How was Debbie's account of what happened to her affecting her life, Fred?
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，黛比对自己遭遇的叙述是如何影响她生活的？

sentences.en: Oh, there's a sadness or a poignancy sometimes when you see people who are hurt like that.
sentences.zh: 哦，当你看到那些受到伤害的人时，有时会感到一种悲伤或辛酸。

sentences.en: Her conversation is about my ex and the lost marriage and what a bad person he was.
sentences.zh: 她的谈话内容总是关于我的前夫、失去的婚姻，以及他是个多么糟糕的人。
但它笼罩在失败的阴影中。
这是一种“这行不通”的感觉。

sentences.en: There were obstacles too big for me.
sentences.zh: 有些障碍对我来说太大了。

sentences.en: And that has implications for her entire life.
sentences.zh: 这对她的整个人生都有影响。

sentences.en: I understand that it was important for her to let everyone else know what a louse her husband was and how much pain he had caused her.
sentences.zh: 我理解她有必要让其他人知道她的丈夫是个混蛋，以及他给她造成了多大的痛苦。

sentences.en: That, that is true for her.
sentences.zh: 那，那对她来说是真实的。

sentences.en: It's like, let me tell you.
Now let me tell you again.
sentences.zh: 现在让我再告诉你一遍。

sentences.en: Now let me call up grandma and tell her.
sentences.zh: 现在让我给奶奶打电话告诉她。

sentences.en: The real suffering is when that failure and that loss become part of their identity.
sentences.zh: 真正的痛苦在于，那种失败和损失成为了他们身份的一部分。

sentences.en: And so for somebody like Debbie, when we had encountered her, it was, hi, I'm Debbie, a woman with a lousy ex-husband and a failed marriage.
sentences.zh: 所以对于像黛比这样的人，当我们遇到她时，她会说：嗨，我是黛比，一个有着糟糕前夫和失败婚姻的女人。

sentences.en: So that had meant that it was now integrated into her self-concept.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着它现在已经融入了她的自我概念中。

sentences.en: In the course of your work and research, you came by another person named Jill.
sentences.zh: 在你的工作和研究过程中，你还遇到了另一个人，名叫吉尔。

sentences.en: And she confided in you about her troubled relationship with her mother.
sentences.zh: 她向你倾诉了她与母亲之间糟糕的关系。

sentences.en: But unlike in the case of Debbie's ex, Jill's mother was dead?
sentences.zh: 但与黛比的前夫的情况不同，吉尔的母亲已经去世了？

sentences.en: And so she was, my mom didn't love me.
sentences.zh: 所以她会说，我妈妈不爱我。

sentences.en: I never got the kind of affection that I would hope for.
sentences.zh: 我从未得到过我所希望的那种关爱。
我感到被拒绝和不受欢迎。

sentences.en: And I grew up with this sense of not being good enough and, you know, not having enough value in this world.
sentences.zh: 我在这种“我不够好”的感觉中长大，你知道，觉得在这个世界上没有足够的价值。

sentences.en: And no matter what I said to mom, I couldn't get through to her.
sentences.zh: 无论我对妈妈说什么，我都无法触动她。

sentences.en: You know, like, mom, notice me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是，妈妈，关注我一下。

sentences.en: And so Jill brought that sense of frustration and invisibleness to the way she talked about what it was that had occurred, you know, 20 years ago when her mother had died.
sentences.zh: 所以吉尔在谈论20年前她母亲去世时发生的事情时，带入了那种挫败感和被忽视感。

sentences.en: You could just feel the angSt.
sentences.zh: 你真的能感受到那种痛苦。

sentences.en: You know, what is striking about both these stories you've just told me, Fred, is that in both Debbie's case and in Jill's case, the source of their pain is in their paSt.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，你刚才讲的这两个故事最引人注目的是，无论是黛比的情况还是吉尔的情况，她们痛苦的根源都在过去。

sentences.en: But it's almost as if this person, this other person, is standing with them, walking with them, living with them inside their heads all the time.
sentences.zh: 但就好像这个人，这个另一个人，一直和她们站在一起，陪她们走，一直活在她们的脑海里。

sentences.en: And they don't realize how integrated that wound or problem has become in their self-identity.
sentences.zh: 她们没有意识到那种创伤或问题已经多么深刻地融入了她们的自我认同中。

sentences.en: And that link, that integration makes it seem really hard to imagine, what would I be without this?
sentences.zh: 而那种联系，那种整合，让人很难想象：如果没有这些，我会是谁？

sentences.en: So you're a scholar, you're a teacher, you're a therapist, but you're also a human being, and you yourself are not invulnerable to holding on to a grievance.
sentences.zh: 所以你是一位学者、老师、治疗师，但你也是一个人，你自己也并非对怀恨在心免疫。

sentences.en: I want you to tell me the story of your friend, Sam, and what happened to you and Sam, and maybe start with how close you were to Sam for many years of your life.
sentences.zh: 我想让你讲讲你朋友山姆的故事，以及你和山姆之间发生了什么，也许可以从你们多年来有多亲密开始讲起。

sentences.en: Sam was my closest friend for probably a decade.
sentences.zh: 山姆大概有十年是我最亲密的朋友。

sentences.en: Somebody I considered, somebody I considered almost a brother and a very, very dear friend of my wife and I.
sentences.zh: 我曾认为他几乎是我的兄弟，也是我和我妻子非常、非常亲爱的朋友。

sentences.en: I assumed that Sam would always hold that place in my life.
sentences.zh: 我以为山姆会永远在我生命中占据那个位置。

sentences.en: So what happened or what transpired was he met someone who was, for whatever reason, uncomfortable with the relationship that Sam had with me and my wife.
sentences.zh: 所以发生了什么，或者说发生了什么事，是他遇到了一个人，无论出于什么原因，那个人对山姆和我及我妻子之间的关系感到不舒服。

sentences.en: We're best friends and now poof.
sentences.zh: 我们是最好的朋友，然后砰的一声，人没了。

sentences.en: And I couldn't connect with him.
And the word ghosted did not exist then, but I was ghosted.
sentences.zh: 当时还没有“被鬼影”这个词，但我确实被“鬼影”了。

sentences.en: And inside of me, I fell apart.
I became bitter as my trust was shattered.
sentences.zh: 随着信任的破碎，我变得痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: And I developed a bit of like an agitated depression.
sentences.zh: 我产生了一种类似焦虑性抑郁的情绪。

sentences.en: I understand that at one point, Fred, you heard that Sam was to be married and you did not hear about this from Sam, but from someone else.
sentences.zh: 我理解在某个时刻，弗雷德，你听说山姆要结婚了，而且你不是从山姆那里听说的，而是从别人那里听说的。

sentences.en: When a mutual friend came to my house and said, oh, by the way, you know, he's getting married.
sentences.zh: 当一位共同的朋友来到我家说，哦，顺便提一下，你知道，他要结婚了。

sentences.en: I had absolutely no ability to integrate that information.
sentences.zh: 我完全没有能力消化这个信息。

sentences.en: It hit me like bricks in my face.
sentences.zh: 它像砖头一样砸在我的脸上。

sentences.en: So you were not invited to the wedding.
sentences.zh: 所以你没有被邀请参加婚礼。

sentences.en: This is someone whom you consider to be, as you said, your best friend, nearly a brother.
sentences.zh: 这可是你认为的，正如你所说，最好的朋友，几乎是兄弟的人。

sentences.en: How did that change your outlook and behavior?
sentences.zh: 这如何改变了你的心态和行为？

sentences.en: I understand that the people around you started to notice that you were different.
sentences.zh: 我理解你周围的人开始注意到你变了。

sentences.en: My wife turned to me one day and said, Fred, I still love you.
sentences.zh: 我妻子有一天转向我说，弗雷德，我依然爱你。

sentences.en: I just don't like you as much.
sentences.zh: 我只是没那么喜欢你了。

sentences.en: So I was, to put it kindly, crabby.
sentences.zh: 所以，说得好听点，我当时很暴躁。

sentences.en: I understand that at one point during the saga, Fred, you found yourself in a very unusual place to have an epiphany, the supermarket.
sentences.zh: 我理解在那个传奇故事的某个时刻，弗雷德，你发现自己在一个非常不寻常的地方有了顿悟，那就是超市。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened at the supermarket that day.
sentences.zh: 告诉我那天在超市发生了什么。

sentences.en: So my wife told me to go to the supermarket.
And I told her I wanted to go to supermarket A because it was closer.
sentences.zh: 我告诉她我想去A超市，因为它更近。

sentences.en: She said, go to supermarket B, Safeway.
I walked out of the door muttering, poor me.
sentences.zh: 我一边嘟囔着“我真可怜”一边走出家门。

sentences.en: I get to Safeway muttering all the time, you know, people don't understand me and really like bitter.
sentences.zh: 我一直嘟囔着到了Safeway，你知道，人们不理解我，真的感觉很苦涩。

sentences.en: I walked to the place with the item that my wife is going to send me to Safeway for and it's not there.
sentences.zh: 我走到我妻子让我去Safeway买的那件商品的地方，结果那里没有。

sentences.en: And my self-pity is like overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 我的自怜情绪简直到了极点。

sentences.en: Like, I could have gone to Albertsons and, you know, why am I here?
sentences.zh: 就像是，我本可以去Albertsons的，你知道，我为什么在这儿？

sentences.en: And nobody loves me and nobody understands me.
sentences.zh: 没人爱我，也没人理解我。

sentences.en: And my self-pity went to a kind of overdrive.
sentences.zh: 我的自怜进入了一种超速状态。

sentences.en: But if there was a moment where it broke, just one moment, I turned away from the shelf where the item was supposed to be and I noticed for the first time I'm in Safeway,
sentences.zh: 但如果说有一个瞬间它破灭了，仅仅是一个瞬间，我从本该放着那件商品的货架前转过身，第一次注意到我是在Safeway，

sentences.en: I literally said to myself, holy s**t, Fred, look what you're missing.
sentences.zh: 我当时真的对自己说，天哪，弗雷德，看看你错过了什么。

sentences.en: You're missing apples and oranges and diapers and that you have the money to pay for this.
sentences.zh: 你错过了苹果、橙子、尿布，还有你本有能力支付这一切的事实。

sentences.en: So I had a voice almost in me that said, pay attention, Fred, pay attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，我内心几乎有个声音在说，注意了，弗雷德，注意了。

sentences.en: I walked out of that supermarket and I was, I was different.
sentences.zh: 走出那家超市时，我变了，我整个人都变了。

sentences.en: For better and worse, people we are close to can affect us in profound ways.
sentences.zh: 无论好坏，我们亲近的人都能对我们产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: Sometimes these effects are fleeting and sometimes they last for years.
sentences.zh: 有时这些影响转瞬即逝，有时却能持续多年。

sentences.en: When we come back, the physiological and psychological effects of holding a grudge.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨怀恨在心带来的生理和心理影响。
您正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: When someone wrongs us, holding a grudge against them almost feels like a form of justice.
sentences.zh: 当有人亏待我们时，对他们怀恨在心感觉就像是一种正义。

sentences.en: But psychologist Fred Luskin says that more often than not, grudges don't hurt the targets of our anger.
sentences.zh: 但心理学家弗雷德·拉斯金表示，通常情况下，怨恨并不会伤害到我们愤怒的对象。
它们伤害的是我们自己。

sentences.en: Fred, we've discussed a few ways in which people can hurt us, but sometimes it's a process that hurts us.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，我们讨论过人们伤害我们的几种方式，但有时伤害我们的其实是一个过程。

sentences.en: One person you worked with was upset she did not get a job promotion.
sentences.zh: 你曾辅导过的一位女士因为没能获得升职而感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Can you tell me Dana's story and what went through her mind?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲达娜的故事以及她当时的想法吗？

sentences.en: Dana is one of the people that even after a decade or more, I still remember.
sentences.zh: 达娜是那种即使过了十年甚至更久，我依然记得的人。

sentences.en: Her issue was that she was a great worker for a local Silicon Valley company who worked above and beyond what anybody could expect from an employee.
sentences.zh: 她的问题在于，她是硅谷一家当地公司的优秀员工，工作表现远超任何人对员工的预期。

sentences.en: And so she had an expectation that that best effort would lead to a promotion.
sentences.zh: 因此她期望这种最佳表现能带来升职。

sentences.en: So after a number of years of getting promoted appropriately, there was a bigger job right ahead of her that she just knew she was the right person for the job and had earned it.
sentences.zh: 在连续几年获得应有的晋升后，她面前出现了一个更大的职位，她深知自己就是那个职位的最佳人选，而且她也理应得到它。

sentences.en: And when she found out that she didn't get that job, she became furious.
sentences.zh: 当她发现自己没能得到那个职位时，她愤怒极了。

sentences.en: I mean, hell hath no fury.
I mean, because she had checked all the boxes.
sentences.zh: 因为她已经满足了所有条件。

sentences.en: So if I understand correctly, Fred, Dana's reaction to not being promoted was the sense that she had wasted 10 years of her life,
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，弗雷德，达娜对没能升职的反应是觉得她浪费了十年的生命，

sentences.en: that all this time and effort she had spent at the company going above and beyond, all of it was wasted effort.
sentences.zh: 觉得她在公司投入的所有时间和精力，那些超越职责范围的努力，全都白费了。

sentences.en: Wasted effort and that she was an idiot for putting in all that effort.
sentences.zh: 不仅是努力白费，她还觉得自己是个傻瓜，竟然付出了那么多努力。

sentences.en: It was a multi-pronged attack towards both her employer and towards herself.
sentences.zh: 这是一场针对她雇主以及她自己的多重攻击。

sentences.en: Let's look at one aspect of the story you just told me.
sentences.zh: 让我们看看你刚才讲的故事中的一个侧面。

sentences.en: So this was an employee who did not get a promotion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个没有获得升职的员工。

sentences.en: Another way of looking at this is to say the company has a number of different priorities.
sentences.zh: 另一种看待方式是说，公司有许多不同的优先事项。

sentences.en: Maybe I don't fully understand all the priorities of the company.
sentences.zh: 也许我并不完全了解公司的所有优先事项。

sentences.en: They've picked somebody else, but it's actually not about me.
sentences.zh: 他们选择了别人，但这其实与我个人无关。

sentences.en: It's just about what the company needed to do at this time.
sentences.zh: 这只是公司在当前阶段需要做出的决定。

sentences.en: Dana heard that, that it's about Dana.
sentences.zh: 达娜听到的却是，这是针对达娜个人的。
这是我的公司，我的工作。

sentences.en: She took the no, the rejection as a personal affront.
sentences.zh: 她把这次拒绝视为一种个人侮辱。

sentences.en: Now, in some ways, it's worth pointing out, of course, that not getting that promotion
sentences.zh: 当然，在某种程度上值得指出的是，没能获得升职

sentences.en: did indeed have personal effects on Dana.
sentences.zh: 确实对达娜产生了个人影响。

sentences.en: It might have affected her life, her finances, maybe even her retirement plan.
sentences.zh: 它可能影响了她的生活、财务，甚至可能是她的退休计划。

sentences.en: So it had consequences in her personal life, Fred.
sentences.zh: 所以它在她的个人生活中产生了后果，弗雷德。

sentences.en: So there's no denying that Dana's body and mind were affected by not getting the job.
sentences.zh: 所以不可否认，达娜的身心确实受到了没能得到这份工作的影响。

sentences.en: What there is room to negotiate is how much of that effect had to do with Dana's expectations,
sentences.zh: 但可以商榷的是，这种影响中有多少与达娜的期望有关，

sentences.en: not just the not getting the job.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是因为没得到那份工作。

sentences.en: I want to talk about another component of grudges, Fred.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈怨恨的另一个组成部分，弗雷德。

sentences.en: You worked with a man named Alan, whose wife cheated on him.
sentences.zh: 你曾辅导过一个叫艾伦的人，他的妻子背叛了他。

sentences.en: Can you tell me his story and the thoughts that constantly circled around in his mind?
sentences.zh: 你能讲讲他的故事以及他脑海中不断盘旋的想法吗？

sentences.en: So Alan had a wife who cheated on him, like, and she didn't, like, try to hide it.
sentences.zh: 艾伦的妻子背叛了他，而且她甚至没想过要隐瞒。

sentences.en: You know, it was like, we're married, but you don't satisfy me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是说，我们结婚了，但你不能满足我。

sentences.en: So, you know, I have an affair.
And she shut him down if he started to complain or articulate his needs.
sentences.zh: 而且当他开始抱怨或表达需求时，她会直接堵住他的话。

sentences.en: So Alan just had one of those, like, doozies of a story.
sentences.zh: 所以艾伦的故事简直是个典型的烂摊子。

sentences.en: The blame is the second piece of a three-part sequence.
sentences.zh: 指责是三部曲中的第二部分。

sentences.en: It starts with taking it too personally, which you covered.
sentences.zh: 它始于过度个人化，这一点你已经讲过了。

sentences.en: When we take things too personally, our mind and body react in a very harsh, physically disruptive,
sentences.zh: 当我们把事情看得太个人化时，我们的身心会以一种非常严苛、生理上具有破坏性，
以及情感上痛苦的方式做出反应。

sentences.en: And then we have to talk to ourselves about what happened.
sentences.zh: 然后我们不得不对自己讲述发生了什么。

sentences.en: So all three of those end up as this quality of blame.
sentences.zh: 所以这三者最终都汇聚成了这种指责的特质。

sentences.en: Same, you did it to me.
sentences.zh: 同样，是你对我做了这些。

sentences.en: I'm not responsible for how bad I feel.
sentences.zh: 我对自己感觉这么糟糕不负责任。

sentences.en: And I'm going to talk to myself.
That solidifies this as a blaming story.
sentences.zh: 这巩固了它作为一个指责故事的地位。

sentences.en: I can see in some ways how, at least on a short-term basis, this can make you feel better.
sentences.zh: 我能理解在某种程度上，至少在短期内，这能让你感觉好受些。

sentences.en: If you're feeling very upset, if you're feeling very hurt,
sentences.zh: 如果你感到非常沮丧，如果你感到非常受伤，

sentences.en: it does make you feel better to say, I know what the cause of my hurt is.
sentences.zh: 说“我知道我痛苦的原因是什么”确实会让你感觉好受些。

sentences.en: This other person did this terrible thing, and that's why I'm feeling terrible.
sentences.zh: 是这个人做了这件可怕的事，所以我才感觉这么糟糕。

sentences.en: Because when people are devastated, it's appropriate to be disrupted, dysregulated,
sentences.zh: 因为当人们遭受打击时，感到混乱、失调、

sentences.en: confused, angry, lost, scared, and short-term,
sentences.zh: 困惑、愤怒、迷茫、恐惧都是正常的，而在短期内，

sentences.en: it's really helpful to have somebody to blame besides you.
sentences.zh: 能有除了自己以外的人可以指责，真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: So we've talked about the role that taking things personally and the blame game plays in the
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了过度个人化和指责游戏在
怨恨形成中所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: These often lead to what you call the final stage in the grievance process, the construction
sentences.zh: 这些通常会导致你所说的怨恨过程的最后阶段，即构建

sentences.en: What do you mean by this, Fred?
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，你这是什么意思？

sentences.en: When something happens, we have a choice of how we talk about it.
sentences.zh: 当事情发生时，我们有权选择如何谈论它。

sentences.en: And so we can talk about it as a normal life event, a catastrophe, something to cope with,
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它当作一个普通的生活事件、一场灾难、需要应对的事情，

sentences.en: you know, something I'm here to learn from, or a sign that the world is an unfair, unsafe place.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是我可以从中学习的东西，或者是一个世界不公平、不安全的信号。

sentences.en: What we lose when we get too deep into a grievance story is, one, we have a choice.
sentences.zh: 当我们深陷怨恨故事时，我们失去的是：第一，我们本可以选择。

sentences.en: So that story of, hey, I got a really crappy deal with this wife, and she messed up my life for six months,
sentences.zh: 所以，那个“嘿，我在这段婚姻里遭遇了糟糕的对待，她毁了我六个月的生活”的故事，

sentences.en: that's a healthy story for a month or so, you know?
sentences.zh: 作为一个月左右的心理调节是健康的，你懂吗？

sentences.en: It's like that's how your brain rebalances and reorganizes itself from the disruption,
sentences.zh: 这就像是你的大脑从混乱中重新平衡和重组的方式，

sentences.en: and it can't go directly to, oh, let's think about this.
sentences.zh: 它不可能直接跳到“哦，让我们思考一下”。

sentences.en: I didn't make a good choice in marriage.
sentences.zh: 我在婚姻中没做出好的选择。

sentences.en: She gave me lots of clues.
You can't reorganize, you know, coherently right away.
sentences.zh: 你不可能立刻连贯地重组，你知道的。

sentences.en: So she's a terrible human being is a wonderful way to reorganize.
sentences.zh: 所以“她是个糟糕的人”是一种极好的重组方式。

sentences.en: The grievance story is a practice for how it is we're going to explain to ourselves what happened
sentences.zh: 怨恨故事是一种练习，用来解释我们自己发生了什么，

sentences.en: and what's an appropriate response for us to deal with it.
sentences.zh: 以及我们该如何应对才是恰当的反应。

sentences.en: The practice of it is very useful short-term and destructive long-term.
sentences.zh: 这种练习在短期内非常有用，但长期来看具有破坏性。

sentences.en: I'm curious why some wrongdoings become grudges and others don't.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇为什么有些委屈会变成怨恨，而有些则不会。

sentences.en: You talk about a very powerful concept, the violation of unenforceable rules.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了一个非常有力的概念，即“不可执行规则的违背”。

sentences.en: When Dana wanted a promotion, she turned what she wanted into an expectation.
sentences.zh: 当达娜想要升职时，她把自己想要的变成了期望。

sentences.en: When somebody gets married, they have a hope, you know, I want my partner to be faithful.
sentences.zh: 当有人结婚时，他们怀有希望，你知道，“我希望我的伴侣忠诚”。

sentences.en: But they change it into they have to be faithful.
sentences.zh: 但他们把它变成了“他们必须忠诚”。

sentences.en: That is a rule for somebody else's behavior that you actually don't have power to enforce.
sentences.zh: 那是对他人的行为所设定的规则，而你实际上并没有权力去强制执行。

sentences.en: If you wake up in the morning and you say, hey, I got a big day today.
sentences.zh: 如果你早上醒来说，嘿，我今天有重要的事情。

sentences.en: It has to be sunny and it's pouring.
sentences.zh: 必须是晴天，结果却下着倾盆大雨。

sentences.en: Most normal people recognize they don't control the weather.
sentences.zh: 大多数正常人都会意识到他们无法控制天气。

sentences.en: But when an adult person does something that you don't want, we bypass that, well, a normal adult person doesn't have to do what I want.
sentences.zh: 但当一个成年人做了你不想要的事情时，我们就会忽略这一点——好吧，一个正常的成年人不必非得按我的意愿行事。

sentences.en: But when we create unenforceable rules, we start thinking an adult separate from me has to do what I want.
sentences.zh: 但当我们创造了不可执行的规则时，我们开始认为一个独立的成年人必须按我的意愿行事。

sentences.en: They have to give me a promotion.
They have to stay, my friend.
sentences.zh: 他们必须留下来，我的朋友。

sentences.en: Or also, they have to talk to me.
sentences.zh: 或者，他们必须和我说话。

sentences.en: Those unenforceable rules are rigid, like substrates in our thinking that when they're broken, cause us to have all sorts of exaggerated distress.
sentences.zh: 那些不可执行的规则是僵化的，就像我们思维中的基质，一旦被打破，就会导致我们产生各种夸张的痛苦。

sentences.en: I want to talk about one unenforceable rule that you had in your life, Fred.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你生活中曾经有过的一条不可执行规则，弗雷德。

sentences.en: When your mother-in-law was alive, you and your family would often go and visit her in Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 你岳母在世时，你和家人经常去康涅狄格州看望她。

sentences.en: I understand that she wasn't very nice to you.
Let's just say it was a relationship challenge.
sentences.zh: 我们姑且称之为一种人际关系挑战吧。

sentences.en: But yes, there was one situation where she demanded that I do something in her home and it was absolutely trivial.
sentences.zh: 但确实有一次，她要求我在她家里做某事，那件事绝对是微不足道的。

sentences.en: It was something along the lines of, don't put this back here.
sentences.zh: 大概是类似“别把这个放回这里”。

sentences.en: You have to put it back here.
And she was yelling at me because I had put it back in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 她对我大吼大叫，因为我把它放错了地方。

sentences.en: So she had an unenforceable, like sons-in-law can't put things back where I don't want them put back.
sentences.zh: 所以她有一条不可执行的规则，比如“女婿不能把东西放在我不希望他们放的地方”。

sentences.en: And then I had an unenforceable rule, moms-in-law can't talk to me like this.
sentences.zh: 然后我有一条不可执行的规则，“岳母不能这样跟我说话”。

sentences.en: I heard myself saying it in my mind.
sentences.zh: 我听到自己在心里这么说。

sentences.en: You can't talk to me like this.
And I ran out the front door.
I literally ran out the front door, ran away from my wife and her family,
sentences.zh: 我真的跑出了前门，逃离了我的妻子和她的家人，

sentences.en: I literally took a run because my unenforceable role was shouting at me.
sentences.zh: 我真的跑开了，因为我那不可执行的规则在对我大喊大叫。

sentences.en: Who is she to do this?
I was gone for like an hour.
sentences.zh: 我离开了一个小时左右。

sentences.en: My wife thought I was crazy enough to have gone back to California.
sentences.zh: 我妻子以为我疯到已经跑回加州去了。

sentences.en: But, and I'm not blaming one shred of this on my mother-in-law.
sentences.zh: 但是，我并没有把这事的一丝一毫归咎于我岳母。

sentences.en: But I'm saying my rule, she broke my rule so strongly that I could only react that way
sentences.zh: 我是说我的规则，她打破了我的规则，以至于我只能那样反应，

sentences.en: because of the rule, not the reality of what she did.
sentences.zh: 是因为那条规则，而不是她所做之事的现实。

sentences.en: So after this fight, I understand that you called a friend to complain about your mother-in-law.
sentences.zh: 所以在那次争吵之后，我听说你给一个朋友打电话抱怨你的岳母。

sentences.en: You wanted to tell someone else your grievance story.
sentences.zh: 你想告诉别人你的怨恨故事。

sentences.en: What did you say and what did your friend tell you?
sentences.zh: 你说了什么，你的朋友又对你说了什么？

sentences.en: And so either during that run or later, I went to the, a pay phone.
sentences.zh: 就在那次跑步期间或之后，我走到了一部公用电话旁。

sentences.en: I didn't want to do it in the house.
sentences.zh: 我不想在家里做这件事。

sentences.en: And I called up really close friends and I started to complain about my mother-in-law.
sentences.zh: 我给非常亲密的朋友打了电话，开始抱怨我的岳母。

sentences.en: And I got about 10 seconds in and the friend said,
sentences.zh: 我大概说了10秒钟，朋友就说，

sentences.en: Fred, every time you go there, you call me to complain.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，你每次去那里，都会打电话给我抱怨。

sentences.en: And, and I looked, I looked at myself and I looked at him and said, but this one's serious.
sentences.zh: 我审视了一下自己，又看了看他，说，但这回是认真的。

sentences.en: And he said, I'm sure it's serious, but every single time you go there,
sentences.zh: 他说，我相信你是认真的，但每次你去那里，

sentences.en: you call us to complain about her and you want us to agree with you.
sentences.zh: 你都会打电话给我们抱怨她，还想让我们同意你的观点。

sentences.en: So complain and we'll agree with you.
sentences.zh: 那就抱怨吧，我们会同意你的。

sentences.en: But understand you do this every time.
sentences.zh: 但你要明白，你每次都这样。
天哪，这个女人控制了我。
她控制了我的神经系统。

sentences.en: They take me to the phone.
sentences.zh: 是它们带我走向电话的。

sentences.en: We've talked about the anatomy of grudges and how they form.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过怨恨的本质以及它们是如何形成的。

sentences.en: Let's spend a moment talking about some of the consequences of holding on to our past grievances.
sentences.zh: 让我们花点时间谈谈沉溺于过去的不满所带来的一些后果。

sentences.en: Many studies have examined the relationship between resentment and mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 许多研究都考察了怨恨与心理健康问题之间的关系。

sentences.en: One study, for example, found that holding a grudge could lead to lower self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 例如，一项研究发现，怀恨在心可能会导致自尊心下降。

sentences.en: I mean, there's lots of information about how hostile thoughts, resentment, and blame are all negatives for long-term physical well-being.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多信息表明，敌对思想、怨恨和指责对长期的身体健康都是负面的。

sentences.en: One of the studies that I liked when I was doing a lot of this was there was a linear relationship between blame and all cause, like physical well-being.
sentences.zh: 我在做这方面的研究时，很喜欢其中一项研究，它发现指责与各种原因导致的身体健康状况之间存在线性关系。

sentences.en: There is a good degree of evidence that hostile people have greater heart disease.
sentences.zh: 有充分的证据表明，充满敌意的人患心脏病的几率更高。

sentences.en: I feel like I can remember times in my own life, Fred, when I've been up at 3.45 in the morning, upset about what someone said to me or what someone did to me.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德，我觉得我能想起自己生活中的某些时刻，当时我凌晨3点45分还醒着，因为别人对我所说或所做的事而感到心烦意乱。

sentences.en: And I'm lying in bed, tossing and turning.
And, of course, it seems like the effects on sleep must be one of the effects of resentment and grievance.
sentences.zh: 当然，怨恨和不满对睡眠的影响似乎是必然的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and there was a recent study that linked what you're calling perseveration and anger.
sentences.zh: 是的，最近有一项研究将你所说的“反刍思维”与愤怒联系了起来。

sentences.en: Both were linked to sleep quality.
sentences.zh: 两者都与睡眠质量有关。

sentences.en: Why is it that grievance and grudges cause these physiological effects?
sentences.zh: 为什么不满和怨恨会引起这些生理反应？

sentences.en: What is happening physiologically to us that cause an effect on sleep, that cause an effect on the heart, that cause an effect on high blood pressure?
sentences.zh: 我们的生理上发生了什么，导致了对睡眠、心脏和高血压的影响？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the clearest and simplest link is with the stress response.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，最清晰、最简单的联系就是压力反应。

sentences.en: So when you're angry or when you're pissed off or when you're blaming, you have an internalized sense of threat.
sentences.zh: 所以当你愤怒、恼火或指责他人时，你内心会有一种威胁感。

sentences.en: Someone out there has hurt you or disappointed you or left you, and you're not okay.
sentences.zh: 外面有人伤害了你、让你失望或抛弃了你，而你感觉不好。

sentences.en: So that sense of not okay, you know, leads the brain and it signals to the adrenals and all sorts of changes to prepare you to, you know, run away.
sentences.zh: 所以那种“感觉不好”的状态，会引导大脑向肾上腺发出信号，并引发各种变化，让你做好逃跑的准备。

sentences.en: They, and run away doesn't have to be physically run away.
sentences.zh: 而且，逃跑不一定非得是身体上的逃跑。

sentences.en: It could be, I'll never talk to them again.
sentences.zh: 它可能是“我再也不跟他们说话了”。

sentences.en: That's a form of flight or fight them, be hostile.
sentences.zh: 那也是一种逃避或对抗的形式，即表现出敌意。

sentences.en: But the more you're angry and the more you're blaming, the more you arouse that system.
sentences.zh: 但你越愤怒、越指责，就越会激发那个系统。

sentences.en: The more you trigger an adrenalized response, the more you train your body to, you know, accommodate cortisol, the more your brain gets used to that pathway of reaction,
sentences.zh: 你越是触发肾上腺素反应，就越是在训练你的身体去适应皮质醇，你的大脑也就越习惯那种反应路径，

sentences.en: You know, it becomes easier to do because the templates become laid down more, you know, succinctly.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这变得更容易了，因为模板被更简洁地固定了下来。

sentences.en: The immediacy of arousal of anything that's a threat to us is the reason why long-term grievances are so dangerous.
sentences.zh: 任何威胁到我们的事物所引发的即时唤醒，正是长期不满如此危险的原因。

sentences.en: So the irony here, Fred, is that grudges can make us feel better in the short term.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的讽刺之处在于，弗雷德，怨恨在短期内能让我们感觉好受些。

sentences.en: They make us feel like we're getting back at the people who've hurt us.

sentences.en: So when our arousal and our physiology and our threats say we need to protect ourselves, anger can be a really good response.

sentences.en: The destructive anger is when anger does not lead to useful action.
sentences.zh: 破坏性愤怒是指愤怒没有转化为有用的行动。

sentences.en: When it just becomes perseverative and in a grievance, it actually becomes a substitute for action.
sentences.zh: 当它仅仅变成一种反刍和不满时，它实际上成了行动的替代品。

sentences.en: In a chronic anger situation, there's a little bit of dopamine that you get, that pleasure chemical.

sentences.en: The dopamine is a response to an anticipated value.

sentences.en: But in anger, you never get that anticipated value unless you actually do something and change.
